new_jobs.description:
Description

The Design, Sustainability and Engineering team in GREF seeks an experienced Program Manager with strong cross-functional leadership skills to own GREF’s Global Furniture Fixtures & Equipment (FF&E) Program. This role is the single point of strategic ownership for FF&E lifecycle management, procurement strategy, asset management, and cross-functional coordination across GREF's worldwide workplace portfolio.

The FF&E function within GREF covers four primary responsibilities: defining and maintaining FF&E standards and strategy, stewarding the Workplace FF&E Standards, driving regional procurement strategies, sustainability, and benchmarking against industry practice to identify gaps and improvements.

This role serves as the connective tissue between Global Design, Workplace Guidelines, Construction delivery teams, GREF Finance, Global Corporate Sustainability, Portfolio Management, and Global Corporate Procurement (GCP). The successful candidate will integrate constraints and requirements from cross-functional stakeholders into efficient, scalable, globally-relevant solutions that are fiscally responsible and advance Amazon's sustainability commitments.

Key job responsibilities

Own the end-to-end FF&E Lifecycle Management Strategy across GREF's global portfolio — from specification and procurement through operations, storage, and end-of-life disposition.
Own and drive the FF&E procurement strategy, partnering with GCP under the shared-accountability model to co-own joint savings commitments while balancing regional availability, sustainability, and cost caps
Own global FF&E Asset Tracking (AST) strategy across all GREF-supported sites, including asset storage, product ordering, inventory management, and evaluation of aging products to meet requirements of 100% inventory coverage and >90% data quality accuracy. Develop and enforce governance, risk and compliance controals for FF&E including monthly verification tracking, sadhbaords scopes and compliance evidence documentation
Establish and maintain furniture asset lifetime guidelines, condition assessment criteria, and refurbishment standards that inform replacement planning, budget forecasting, and warranty alignment
Collaborate in develop and manage a global FF&E circularity program — identifying, cataloging, and redistributing surplus assets to avoid unnecessary new purchases; establish partnerships with internal reuse functions, donation, resale, takeback programs and recycling partners for end-of-life disposition
Own the GREF Workplace FF&E Standards (selection, testing, digital catalog) and FF&E Guidelines (design guidance, trade up/down decision logic, playbooks for internal and external teams)
Develop the FF&E technology strategy, inclusive of disposal method tracking, including evaluating and driving decisions on platform capabilities, integration architecture across regional systems, and AI-enabled asset discovery tools
Benchmark industry best practices, identify gaps between Global Workplace Design Guidelines and regional trends, and provide solution-oriented recommendations
Lead cross-functional stakeholder alignment across Design, Construction, MAC, Portfolio Management, Procurement, Finance, IT, AV, Security, and sustainability teams
Develop cost-avoidance tracking and reporting to quantify savings from procurement consolidation, reuse programs, and vendor strategy; coordinate environmental impact reporting (waste diversion, embodied carbon reduction)

A day in the life

This role is deeply cross-functional. You'll partner daily with Design, Construction, Procurement, Finance, Sustainability, Portfolio Management, and regional operations teams — aligning competing priorities into one global strategy for how Amazon's furniture is specified, procured, tracked, reused, and retired. One conversation might be negotiating a global seating contract; the next, advancing a circular economy partnership or troubleshooting asset data quality with a regional lead across the world. You own the system end-to-end, and you'll measure impact in millions saved and tons diverted from landfill.

About The Team

The Global Real Estate and Facilities (GREF) team manages Amazon's real estate and facilities globally. It's organized into Regional Portfolio Management, Global Centers of Enablement, and Global Centers of Expertise. Design, Sustainability and Engineering includes Global Design, Workplace Guidelines, Sustainability, and Engineering teams. These teams develop design concepts, implement workplace standards, and deliver various spaces across Amazon's portfolio. GREF emphasizes inclusive team culture, work-life balance, and career growth. The team values diversity and promotes knowledge sharing and mentorship. GREF strives to create spaces that support Amazonians' work while enhancing employee well-being and aligning with the company's strategic vision.

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements

Master's degree
Knowledge of financial asset classification including capitalization thresholds and Special Economic Zone compliance implications for asset registries
Experience designing, implementing, and scaling upskilling, apprenticeship, or workforce development programs across large-scale operations or corporate environments, including forecasting workforce needs and leveraging analytics to drive program decisions

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Workforce Development, Aging and Community Services
new_jobs.description:
Position/Program Information

EXAM NUMBER

AG8194B-R

TYPE OF RECRUITMENT

We welcome applications from anyone.

WHEN TO APPLY

We will be accepting online applications from Wednesday, September 23, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. (PT) until Monday, September 28, 2026, 5:00 PM (PT).

All applications must be received before 5:00 p.m. (PT) on Monday, September 28, 2026, to be accepted.

WHY WORK FOR US?

The Aging and Disabilities Department (AD) serves the growing population of older adults, dependent adults, and individuals with disabilities in Los Angeles County. The department offers a broad range of services aimed at fostering dignity, independence, and overall well-being. Through compassionate and intentional support, AD ensures that individuals can live fulfilling lives within their communities, maintaining the highest quality of life possible. We partner with non-profits, community-based organizations, commissions, and other government agencies to provide services such as social, educational and recreational services, training and education programs, accessibility services, wellness and nutrition programs, emergency preparedness and response programs, home-delivery meal services, in-home visiting programs, crisis intervention, legal services involving fraud, abuse, neglect, exploitation, and other issues that pertain to the older and dependent adults in the community.

Essential Job Functions

Plans, organizes, assigns, and coordinates the work of the organizational unit, resolving policy issues and problems as they arise.
Advises department administration on policy issues involving the work of the organizational unit.
Has responsibility for major administrative functions such as budget, accounting, personnel, or internal support services.
Develops and implements solutions to complex problems of organization, budget, personnel, or procedures that occur within the Program Manager's area of responsibility.
Plans, organizes, and directs the work of subordinate staff in: Development of comprehensive plans and service priorities for Departmental programs; Development of contractor selection and contracting systems; Management of contract monitoring and compliance mechanisms; Working with advisory bodies and the public to elicit the opinions and advice of these interested parties.
Directs Senior and Service Center managers and staff in the delivery of direct services to the public.
Formulates recommendations of departmental policies and procedures.
Maintains liaison with a variety of officials, agencies, and organizations in complex or high level matters concerning the Department.
Coordinates the work of the organizational unit with that of other County departments and divisions.
Represents the department before subcommittees and full meetings of various advisory councils, workshops, conferences, and meetings of special committees.

For more information, please view the classification specification: Program Manager, Workforce Development, Aging and Community Services

Requirements

REQUIREMENTS TO QUALIFY

OPTION 1
One (1) year of experience at the level of Los Angeles County's class of Project Supervisor, Community Services* , or higher, responsible for the development and/or implementation of community development and older adult services or related programs**.

OPTION 2

Three (3) years of experience at the level of Los Angeles County's class of Community Center Director I* ** , or higher, one (1) year of which must include supervision during the last three (3) years, participating in the development and/or implementation of community development and older adult services or related programs** or in departmental administrative support functions.

OPTION 3

Three (3) years of experience in a highly responsible administrative capacity**** analyzing and making recommendations for the solution of problems of organization, financial services, human resources, or information technology, one (1) year of which must have been at the level of Los Angeles County's class of Administrative Services Manager III*****, directing or assisting in directing an administrative, human resources, financial services, or information technology program unit in the service of Los Angeles County.

Special Requirement Information

Project Supervisor, Community Services is defined as having responsibility for supervising a special project involving the development and implementation of service programs that require direct community participation. Qualifying experience at this level must include responsibility for planning, developing, implementing, coordinating, and/or evaluating community-based service programs, rather than solely supervising staff, volunteers, events, or routine program activities.
Community development and older adult services or related programs refers to organized programs designed to address community needs or provide services to older adults and other targeted populations. Such programs may include, but are not limited to, community engagement and outreach, older adult services, social or supportive services, health and wellness programs, educational or recreational programs, resource and referral services, or other programs intended to improve access to services and community well-being.
Community Center Director I is defined as serving as the administrative head of a diversified, multi-service community center or older adult services center.
Highly responsible administrative capacity is defined as administrative work involving substantial responsibility for analyzing, evaluating, developing, and/or recommending solutions to complex organizational, financial services, human resources, or information technology problems, policies, procedures, programs, or operations. Qualifying experience must require the exercise of significant independent judgment, analytical ability, discretion, and responsibility in making recommendations or decisions that affect departmental programs or operations.
*Administrative Services Manager III is defined as directing a section composed of multiple units responsible for providing administrative services that directly impact the management of major departmental programs and operations.

Note:
You may still qualify even if your job title isn’t exactly the same as the ones listed. What matters is that your experience is at a similar level — meaning your job involves similar responsibilities, requires comparable skills and knowledge, and takes place within a similar organizational structure. Please provide a clear explanation of your experience to demonstrate that it is at the appropriate level.

Withhold Information

No withholds will be allowed. Required experience must be fully met and indicated on the application by the last day of filing, and clearly indicated on the application.

Endorsement Of County Qualifications

If you’re a County employee that performed work that differs from the duties described in your class specification and believe you qualify for this opportunity, please provide verification via official documentation of additional responsibility bonus, out-of-class bonus, temporary assignment bonus or reclassification study with CEO Classification within seven (7) calendar days from the last day of filing. Employees do not need to submit such verification if they hold or have held a position that regularly performs functions in alignment with the requirements.

License

A valid California Class C Driver License or the ability to use an alternative method of transportation when needed to carry out job-related essential functions.

Physical Class

2 – Light: This class includes administrative and clerical positions requiring light physical effort that may include occasional light lifting to a 10-pound limit and some bending, stooping, or squatting. Considerable ambulation may be involved.

Additional Information

OUR ASSESSMENT PROCESS

Once we have identified that you meet our requirements, an invitation regarding the following assessment process will be sent:

Examination Content

This examination will consist of a multiple-choice and simulation assessment, worth 100% assessing:

Management Judgement
Willingness to Learn
Empathy
Working Relationships
Sharing Knowledge and Guidance
Analyzing Information
Learning Quickly
Generating New Ideas
Using time Efficiently
Working to High Quality Standards
Adapting to Change
Controlling Emotions
Achievement
Responsibility
Management Potential
Deductive Reasoning
Reading Comprehension

Applicants must receive a passing score of 70% or higher on the assessment to be added to the

list.

Exam Review

STANDARDIZED MULTIPLE CHOICE TESTS ARE NOT REVIEWABLE BY CANDIDATES PER CIVIL SERVICE RULE 7.19 .

Transfer of Test Components

If you have taken identical components recently for other exams, your responses may be automatically transferred to this examination. This exam contains test components that might be used on future exams, and your responses could be transferred to that exam.

Test preparation

We provide study guides and other test preparation resources to help candidates prepare for employment tests. While the guides may help in preparing for the test, we recommend reviewing all related materials that seem necessary.

Online practice tests are available at https://www.shldirect.com/en-us/practice-tests. You can also visit our Los Angeles County Online Assessment Preparation Series webpage at https://lacounty.attract.neogov.com/la-county-online-assessments-prep-series for information about common online assessment types, sample questions, and test-taking tips.
Various information can be found on our website at https://hr.lacounty.gov/job-search-toolkit/ . The section dedicated to test preparation is "Employment Test Assistance."

Eligibility and Vacancy Information

Applicants who passed the assessment are placed on a list for a period of six (6) months. We will use this list to fill vacancies in the Department of Aging and Disabilities as they occur.

Application and Filing information

We only accept applications filed online. Applications submitted by U.S. mail, fax, or in person are not accepted. Apply online by clicking on the "Apply" green button at the top right of this posting. This website can also be used to get application status updates.

Please fill out the application completely. Provide relevant job experience including employer's name and address, job title, beginning and ending dates, number of hours worked per week, and description of work performed.

We may verify information included in the application at any point during the examination and hiring process, including after an appointment has been made. Falsification of information could result in refusal of application or rescission of appointment. Copying verbiage from the Requirements or class specification as your work experience will not be sufficient to demonstrate meeting the requirements. Doing so may result in an incomplete application and may lead to disqualification.

We will send notifications to the email address provided on the application, so it is important that you provide a valid email address. If you choose to unsubscribe or opt out from receiving our emails, it is possible to view notices by logging into governmentjobs.com and checking the profile inbox. It is every applicant's responsibility to take steps to view correspondence, and we will not consider claims of missing notices to be a valid reason for re-scheduling an exam part. Register the below domains as approved senders to prevent email notifications from being filtered as spam/junk mail.

ealcazar@hr.lacounty.gov
gtung@hr.lacounty,gov
info@governmentjobs.com
talentcentral@shl.com

New email addresses need to be verified. This only needs to be done once per email address and can be done at any time by logging in to governmentjobs.com and following the prompts. This is to enhance the security of the online application and to prevent incorrectly entered emai

About Plug

Plug is an automotive fintech startup building the marketplace for electric vehicles. Consumers, dealers, and commercial partners trade in, sell, and auction used EVs through a platform built exclusively for electric, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.

Consumers can get an instant cash offer in minutes, backed by data-driven pricing, battery state-of-health analysis, with pickup, payment, and title transfer handled end-to-end. Franchise and independent dealers across the United States bid in real time on inventory sourced directly from these consumers, dealers, and commercial partners. The result is a single platform that gives sellers a fast, fair exit and gives dealers a dedicated channel for sourcing used EV inventory.

Founded in 2023 and led by former Tesla executives, Plug has facilitated $100M in EV sales since launch and is backed by a $20M Series A from Lightspeed Venture Partners. We're building the most AI-native startup team in Los Angeles, full of operators, engineers, and ML researchers laying the transaction rails for the used EV market's exponential growth.

Why Plug

You'll own a piece of the biggest infrastructure opportunity in automotive.
You'll work on a platform built exclusively for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.
You'll be part of an AI-native company. We're rethinking how work gets done at a fundamental level.
You'll work directly with operators who have scaled multi-billion dollar businesses in automotive, EV, and marketplaces.
You'll have real ownership, high autonomy, and a direct line to company outcomes.

The Opportunity

You'll report to the Director of Business Operations and be the go-to person for turning data into decisions. You'll build and maintain the dashboards and models that track how the business is performing, prepare the analysis and slides that go in front of leadership, and use AI tools - including building your own lightweight agents and automations over time - to enhance your workflow and support broader AI adoption across the organization.

You'll support the Director of BizOps on cross-functional initiatives and KPI tracking, bringing depth and speed on the numbers to the work.

What You’ll Own

Analytics & Reporting

Build and maintain BI dashboards (Metabase/Snowflake or equivalent) covering auction performance, dealer operations, vehicle flow, and pricing
Define and track success metrics for BizOps-led initiatives, so leaders always know whether a project is actually working
Build clear, exec-ready slides and reports for recurring leadership reviews

AI & Workflow Automation

Use AI tools to speed up and automate recurring analysis and reporting work.
Build lightweight agents or automated pipelines for repeatable requests.
Bring a builder's mindset to your own workflow and workflow of other teams

Analysis & Business Partnership

Run deep-dive analyses to explain why a metric moved
Translate data into a clear point of view for non-technical stakeholders

What You Are

2-3 years of experience in business operations, data analytics, strategy & ops, or a similarly analytical role (marketplace or automotive experience a plus, not required).
Hands-on comfort building dashboards in a BI tool (Metabase, Tableau, Power BI, or equivalent).
Curiosity and hands-on comfort with AI tools for analysis and workflow automation
Strong slide-building and communication skills — you can turn a messy dataset into something a VP can read in ten seconds.
Business acumen: you understand why a metric matters to the business, not just how to compute it.
Build the analytical backbone of a company at the center of the EV transition.
Ship work quickly and see the impact of your analysis show up in real decisions, fast.
Work directly with operators who've scaled multi-billion-dollar businesses in automotive, EV, and marketplaces.
Join a team that values clarity, ownership, and a bias toward action.

Compensation And Benefits

new_jobs.title: Principal Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Assured is on a mission to modernize insurance. Claims processing (i.e. should we pay this claim?), while often overlooked, is the foundation of the entire industry. It’s currently highly manual, involving phone calls, faxes, and gut instinct, costing tens of billions of dollars a year. We can do better.

At Assured, we provide large insurers with the software solutions they need to win in a modern, technology-driven world. From self-service claim-filing software to backend fraud detection, we’re the engine that powers claims processing for some of the largest insurers in the world.

The challenges we face are deep and diverse, from creating digital experiences that provide comfort and clarity to claimants at their most stressed and vulnerable to orchestrating large-scale ML-driven decision-making on billions of dollars of claims payments, life at Assured is dynamic, collaborative, and rewarding.

We’re looking for an experienced Principal Program Manager
to join our Client Engagement team.

In this role, you’ll help turn complex client priorities into clear, executable programs across Client Engagement, Product, Engineering, and client stakeholders. You’ll own the operating rhythm for high-stakes client initiatives, from kickoff and scoping through launch, adoption, and long-term success.

This is a role for someone who can bring structure to ambiguity, keep cross-functional work moving, and build trust with both internal teams and enterprise customers.

P&C insurance industry experience is a strong plus, but not required. What matters most is the ability to learn the domain quickly and build credibility with enterprise clients.

Some of the Work You’ll Own:

🔗 Turn client needs into clear execution plans.

Sit between Product, Engineering, and client stakeholders to translate client priorities into scoped initiatives, owners, timelines, risks, and next steps.

🚀 Drive high-stakes carrier initiatives from kickoff to launch.

Own the operating plan for client-facing projects, including dependencies, decision points, launch readiness, stakeholder alignment, and the many details that determine whether a rollout feels controlled or chaotic.

📋 Build the Client Engagement operating muscle.

Create the intake, tracking, status, and escalation rhythms that help Client Engagement manage carrier work consistently as Assured scales.

🧭 Make risks and tradeoffs visible early.

When timelines shift, scope expands, or dependencies get stuck, surface the issue clearly, frame the options, and help the right people make the right call before it becomes a client-facing fire drill.

🗣️ Be the translator across clients and internal teams.

Turn carrier feedback, asks, and concerns into clear internal action. Turn Product and Engineering constraints into client-ready explanations that build confidence instead of confusion.

🔍 Find patterns across client work.

Notice when multiple carriers are asking for the same thing, running into the same friction, or needing the same support, and help turn those patterns into better processes, product improvements, or scalable client programs.

⏱️ Keep multiple concurrent initiatives balanced and honest.

Manage the mechanics that keep complex work moving, including RAID logs, dependency mapping, launch plans, follow-ups, status reporting, and critical path management, without adding process for process’s sake.

How You'll Make an Impact:

🎯 Improve confidence in client delivery.

Help Assured give enterprise clients clearer visibility, tighter execution, and more predictable launches across complex initiatives. You’ll build trust by being organized, precise, and honest about what is known, unknown, and changing.

🔍 Keep everyone aligned without meeting overload.

Build clear status updates, trackers, launch plans, and decision logs so leadership, Client Engagement, Product, Engineering, and client stakeholders can understand where things stand without needing another meeting just to find the answer.

⚡ Use AI to move faster.

Use tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and similar platforms to draft project plans, synthesize client feedback, maintain documentation, identify risks, and keep work moving without letting coordination consume the week.

📈 Help scale Client Engagement.

As Assured grows, Client Engagement needs better systems for managing client commitments, launches, escalations, and cross-functional work. You’ll help build the operating model that lets the team scale without losing the high-touch client experience.

You'll Probably Thrive Here If You:

🏗️ Have deep program management experience.

You’ve led complex, cross-functional work with real stakeholder pressure, shifting timelines, ambiguous requirements, and external customers in the mix. You know how to create structure, drive alignment, and keep teams moving when the path is not perfectly defined.

💬 Are client-facing and internally rigorous.

You can communicate clearly with client stakeholders, then turn around and drive internal follow-through with the right level of detail.

🛠️ Are comfortable being technical-adjacent.

You don’t need to write code, but you need to understand product and engineering constraints well enough to ask good questions, scope honestly, and avoid hand-wavy commitments.

🧭 Can operate without waiting for perfect clarity.

You know how to create structure when the path is still forming. You can identify what matters, what’s blocked, who owns what, and what decision needs to happen next.

⚖️ Balance urgency with discipline.

You move quickly, but you don’t skip the basics: owners, dates, risks, dependencies, decisions, and follow-up.

🗣️ Lead through influence.

You know how to get people moving together by being clear, trusted, and relentlessly organized.

🔄 Learn the domain fast.

Prior insurance experience is helpful, but curiosity and speed of learning matter more. You should be able to quickly understand claims workflows, carrier operations, product behavior, and the client context behind each request.

new_jobs.title: Mid Market Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Harbor IT is a leading Managed Service Provider (MSP) specializing in delivering cutting edge Cybersecurity, IT, and Cloud Services to a diverse portfolio of clients. We pride ourselves on our commitment to excellence, innovation, and customer satisfaction. Harbor IT is backed by investment firm Worklyn Partners since 2022 and has built a national platform through acquisition and rapid organic growth. Our mission is to manage our clients’ technology and mitigate their cyber risks, so that they don’t have to.

The Mid-Market Program Manager owns the end-to-end operational performance of Harbor IT's mid-market POD: the clients in it, the delivery staff who serve them, the projects running inside it, and the service delivery workflows that hold it together. This is a true operational leadership role. The Program Manager sets the standard, builds the playbook, and holds the team accountable to it. This is a foundational hire. The POD is being stood up ahead of a significant mid-market client coming online, and the person in this seat is expected to arrive with proven MSP/IT practices and install them, not wait to be handed a process. They will directly manage the POD's Service Delivery Managers, Technical Leads, and support staff; own service quality and SLA attainment; run the POD's PMO and project delivery; own PSA data integrity and the financial inputs of delivery; and carry renewal accountability for the POD book. This role demands a results-oriented operator: someone who holds the team to timelines, enforces standards without apology, and drives outcomes rather than consensus. We do not want a yes-man. We want someone who will push back when the work is not up to standard and own the result either way. The metrics at the end of this document are the job, not an appendix to it.

Organizational Structure

Harbor IT is organized into Practices, which are vertical groupings aligned to client segment: Healthcare, Critical Infrastructure, and Private Equity. Each Practice contains multiple PODs, which are tightly focused delivery units responsible for a defined client set. The POD is the core operating unit of the business. This role leads the mid-market POD and reports into its Practice.

The Mid-Market Program Manager reports directly to the Practice Director, who oversees all PODs within the Practice and is accountable for Practice-level performance and client retention.

Each POD also includes a POD-CIO (virtual CIO, the senior client-facing executive technology partner) and a CSM (Client Success Manager). Neither reports to the Mid-Market Program Manager. The POD-CIO owns executive client relationships, strategic IT roadmaps, and expansion positioning. The CSM handles day-to-day client operations and satisfaction. The Program Manager owns renewal execution and a defined renewal target for the POD book, with pricing and discount authority within limits set by leadership, and is jointly accountable with the POD-CIO for expansion attainment. The Program Manager and POD-CIO are expected to operate in lockstep, aligned daily on client health, escalations, at-risk accounts, and service quality. A breakdown in that partnership will surface immediately in client outcomes.

Ownership Boundaries

Practice Director: Practice-level performance across all PODs, client retention at the Practice level, and the Program Manager's performance.
Mid-Market Program Manager: POD delivery performance, SLA and KPI attainment, the delivery team, the POD's PMO and project outcomes, PSA data integrity, delivery margin inputs, and renewal execution.
POD-CIO: Executive client relationships, strategic IT roadmap, technology standards guidance, and expansion positioning.
CSM: Day-to-day client operations, satisfaction signals, and routine client communication.

Key Responsibilities

Manage and lead the pod's Service Delivery Managers, Technical Leads, and support staff, including hiring, performance management, coaching, and day-to-day workload assignment.
Own service quality for the POD: monitor service levels and enforce compliance with contractual SLAs and KPIs, and define the measurement where it does not yet exist.
Own end-to-end delivery of projects within the pod, including scoping, planning, resourcing, and budget tracking, from kickoff through closeout.
Own queue health for the POD: ticket aging, backlog disposition, escalation rates, reopen rates, and first contact resolution. Review the backlog weekly and disposition every aged ticket.
Own PSA hygiene for the POD: enforce ticket quality standards (notes, categorization, resolution documentation), time entry accuracy and timeliness, and correct work type classification. The Program Manager is accountable if the data in the PSA is wrong.
Own the financial inputs of POD delivery: drive delivery staff utilization to target, enforce 95 percent or better time entry accuracy, manage agreement utilization, identify out-of-scope billing opportunities, and ensure contract compliance. This role directly impacts service margin.
Build and maintain service delivery SOPs, escalation playbooks, ticket handling standards, and onboarding documentation for the POD. This role is expected to create operational structure, not inherit it.
Analyze ticketing and incident trends, identify root causes, and drive remediation through proactive service improvement, delivering a defined number of CSI (continual service improvement) actions each quarter.
Own client communication during major incidents, planned maintenance, and other impactful events, and own the post-incident RCA and follow-through on corrective actions.
Maintain a current performance scorecard for every direct report, with individual metrics that ladder up to POD-level KPIs, and conduct regular 1:1s, performance reviews, and accountability conversations.
Serve as the leader of PMO for the pod, establishing and enforcing consistent project management standards, templates, and reporting across all active pod projects.
Compliment the CX function, partnering on the cadence of client touchpoints and relationship health signals such as CSAT and NPS, and jointly driving proactive action on at-risk accounts.
Join client SBRs and project status reviews for the pod's mid-market accounts, packaging performance, project, and relationship data into a single client-facing narrative.
Monitor program and project-level performance metrics, ticket queues, and incident trends across the pod, and escalate risks before they affect delivery or the client relationship.
Act as the senior escalation point for project, technical, and client issues within the pod and following proper escalation path when an issue exceeds pod-level authority.
Partner with other departments on scoping new project work, contract renewals, and onboarding new mid-market clients into the pod.
Track project and program budgets, resource allocation, and utilization across the pod, and flag variances to leadership.
Apply ITIL-aligned processes and Harbor IT SOPs consistently across the pod's projects and service delivery, and drive continuous improvement across all disciplines in the pod.
Maintain accurate project and program documentation, and keep the pod's SOPs current.

Qualifications & Skills

Proven people leadership as the formal manager of technical or service delivery staff, including hiring, performance reviews, and authority over formal performance improvement or termination decisions. MSP or IT services delivery experience required, not preferred.
Experience managing both projects and ongoing service delivery in an MSP or IT services environment, supporting mid-market clients.
Comfortable carrying commercial accountability, including renewal targets and pricing or discount decisions within defined limits.
Working technical fluency sufficient to handle escalations and represent the POD credibly on technical matters, without needing to be the deepest specialist in the room.
Working knowledge of project management methodology, such as waterfall or agile/hybrid approaches, as well as ITIL service management principles.
Demonstrated experience owning client experience or relationship health metrics, such as CSAT, NPS, or SBR cadence, for a book of accounts, ideally in partnership with a Customer Success function.
Strong organizational skills, with the ability to run multiple concurrent client projects while also managing a team's day-to-day performance.
Comfortable interpreting service and project performance data and packaging it into clear, client-ready reporting.
Demonstrated ownership of contractual SLA and KPI targets, including client-facing reporting against those targets and a specific example of recovering from a miss.
Hands-on configuration or administration experience in a PSA or ITSM platform (ConnectWise, Autotask, HaloPSA, Kaseya BMS, ServiceNow, or comparable): ticket queues, SLA rules, workflows, and performance reporting. Not solely working tickets inside one.
Track record of building service delivery frameworks, SOPs, or operational playbooks in an MSP environment, not just executing someone else's.
Comfortable delivering hard messages to clients and to direct reports without softening them into mush, and willing to push back when work is not up to standard.
Strong communication skills and executive presence, both client-facing and internal.
Enough financial literacy to own program budgets, resource utilization, and a renewal or expansion number.
Comfortable operating as a foundational hire in a fast-paced, growth-stage environment with an evolving scope.

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.
6 to 8 years of experience combining program or project management with service delivery management within an MSP, MSSP, or IT services provider, including at least 2 years as the formal manager of technical or service delivery staff.
PMP or CAPM preferred given ownership of the pod's PMO function.
ITIL v4 Foundations certification a plus.
Prior exposure to technical service delivery, such as NOC, help desk, or infrastructure support, a plus given the technical escalation scope of this role.

KPIs and Performance Metrics

These are the numbers this role is measured on, reviewed monthly with the Practice Director. Baselines are established in the first 60 days and targets are in force from the start of the second full quarter. Establishing the measurement itself is a Day 1 deliverable, not a reason to defer accountability.

Service Quality
SLA attainment: 95 percent or better of tickets and incidents resolved within contractual SLA timeframes
Clean resolution rate: 90 percent or better resolved without escalation or reopen
Escalation rate: 10 percent or less of total tickets requiring Tier 2+ or urgent escalation
First contact resolution: 70 percent or better
Operational Efficiency and Queue Health
Aged ticket backlog: 5 percent or less of open tickets aged beyond SLA threshold
RCA discipline: 98 percent or better of major incidents with a documented RCA within 5 business days
CSI actions: 6 proactive service improvement actions per quarter
Queue review: backlog reviewed and every aged ticket dispositioned weekly, 100 percent
PSA Hygiene and Financial Accuracy
Time entry accuracy: 95 percent or better, correct work type, agreement, and time logged within SLA, measured weekly in the PSA
Ticket quality score: 90 percent or better on a monthly sampled audit of notes, categorization, and resolution documentation
Delivery staff utilization: 70 percent or better, measured weekly
Out-of-scope capture: 100 percent identified and dispositioned, billed or documented as goodwill, within the month incurred
Program and Project Delivery
Schedule performance: 90 percent or better of POD projects delivered within the approved schedule baseline
Budget performance: 95 percent or better delivered within approved budget, plus or minus 5 percent variance

Company Description

It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive. As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care, our technologies like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.

Were a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.

The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.

The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.

If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.

Primary Function of Position:

The Senior Project Manager is responsible for leading and executing the full product development lifecycle of medical device endoscopes and end to end vision pipeline, from initial concept through commercial launch. This role requires deep expertise in medical device development, regulatory pathways, operations, sterilization, biocompatibility, and cross-functional project management. The Senior Project Manager serves as a key driver of product innovation, compliance, and operational excellence within the organization. The Senior Project Manager leads cross-functional execution across all phases of product development, from concept through commercial launch, including concept generation, design, prototyping, verification and validation, regulatory submissions, manufacturing transfer, and launch. The role is pivotal in ensuring that all products meet stringent compliance requirements, including FDA, EU MDR, ISO standards, and relevant quality system regulations.

Execute development plans aligned with product roadmap objectives.
Develop project execution plans, development milestones, and cross-functional plans for Endoscope development programs.
Facilitate program reviews and decision-making discussions with functional and senior leaders to resolve issues, align priorities, and maintain program momentum.

Maintain clear project plans, schedules, risks, and resource allocation.
Partner with engineering teams to drive development of optical, mechanical, illumination, imaging, and sterilization solutions that meet product performance requirements.

Lead comprehensive risk management across multiple workstreams by ensuring risks are identified, analyzed, prioritized, communicated, and used to inform trade-off decisions.
Translate technical, regulatory, operational, and business content into accessible written and oral communications for varied audiences, including reports, project updates, decision summaries, and leadership deliverables.

Ensure smooth transition from R&D to operations with strong cross-functional integration and documentation rigor.
Support ongoing product lifecycle, cost reductions, reliability improvements, and sustainment workstreams.
Partner with Finance and functional leaders to validate financial assumptions, provide budget inputs across workstreams, monitor project financials, and manage trade-offs to remain within approved commitments.

Regulatory & Compliance

Ensure project deliverables meet relevant US and global medical device standards and quality system requirements.
Coordinate cross-functional preparation of regulatory documentation and testing.
Champion strong design controls, risk management, and audit-ready documentation throughout the lifecycle.

In-depth knowledge of medical device regulatory pathways (FDA, EU MDR, ISO 13485), submission requirements, and quality system regulations.
Experience collaborating with engineering, operations, regulatory, quality, and clinical teams throughout all development phases.
Exceptional communication and stakeholder-management skills.
Ability to handle ambiguity effectively and oversee multiple medium size projects at once
Strong organizational skills, including planning, prioritization, and risk management.

Preferred

Experience in robotic surgery, laparoscopic endoscopes, or electro-mechanical medical devices.
PMP certification or formal project management training.
Familiarity with ALM/PLM systems, Agile methodologies, and project management tools.
Expertise in operations, manufacturing processes, sterilization methods (e.g., EtO, autoclave, gamma), and biocompatibility assessment.
